- Exposure to TMR/Main Roads projects and standards
- Strong technical skills and attention to detail
- Ability to work collaboratively within a multidisciplinary team
- Relevant experience in transport infrastructure, road design or civil engineering projects

At Spiire, our purpose is to better our communities, create opportunities for our people and clients, and deliver value to our stakeholders.
We bring together civil and water engineers, landscape architects, construction consultants, surveyors, town planners and urban designers to support the property and infrastructure sectors.
With over 430 employees, we’re one of Australia’s largest employee-owned property and infrastructure consultancies, bringing over 40 years of experience and local expertise to projects across Melbourne, Bendigo, Brisbane, Adelaide, Canberra, Geelong, Ballarat, Shepparton, Gippsland, Albury and Wodonga, and Townsville.
Hello – Kia Ora – 你好 – Wominjeka – Yaama.
No matter how you say it, we’re glad you’re here!
Build your civil career in Townsville
We’re looking for a Civil Designer to join our growing Townsville team and contribute to the design and delivery of urban development and civil infrastructure projects.
You’ll bring experience in urban development civil engineering design, with an interest in working across the different elements of land development. From roads and drainage to earthworks and servicing, you’ll help develop practical, coordinated designs that support projects from concept through to detailed documentation and delivery.
Working closely with our local team and supported by Spiire’s broader network, you’ll take responsibility for work that reflects your experience and strengths. We’re open to Civil Designers with an established foundation in design through to experienced practitioners looking for variety and the opportunity to contribute to a growing team.
This role will see you:
 - Prepare civil engineering designs, drawings and documentation for urban development projects.
 - Contribute to road, drainage, earthworks and servicing design, considering authority requirements and practical construction outcomes.
 - Coordinate inputs from engineers, designers and other project disciplines.
 - Liaise with clients, consultants and authorities to progress designs and address technical requirements.
 - Help resolve design queries and provide engineering input as projects move into construction.
 - Manage agreed tasks, project priorities and timeframes, seeking technical advice when needed.
 - Build strong working relationships and contribute to Spiire’s growing presence in Townsville.
About you
You’re an established Civil Designer with relevant experience in civil infrastructure design, ideally within urban development consulting.
You’ll bring a practical understanding of how the different elements of a development fit together, along with the ability to prepare clear, accurate designs and work collaboratively to resolve project challenges.
You’ll bring:
 - Associates Degree in Civil Engineering is preferred however not mandatory
 - Experience designing civil infrastructure for urban development or land development projects.
 - AutoCAD skills, with experience using 12d highly regarded.
 - An understanding of relevant engineering standards, council requirements and authority approval processes.
 - The ability to prepare and interpret engineering drawings, calculations and technical documentation.
 - Clear communication skills and the ability to build positive relationships with colleagues, clients and project stakeholders.
 - A practical approach to problem-solving and the judgement to recognise when specialist input is needed.
 - The ability to organise your work, follow through on commitments and work with a degree of independence appropriate to your experience.

Make a local impact, backed by a broader team
This is an opportunity to contribute to Spiire’s growing Townsville team and see the impact of your work in the local community.
You’ll work closely with experienced local colleagues while drawing on the technical expertise and support of our broader network. As the team grows, you’ll have opportunities to broaden your project experience, take on responsibility and develop your career in a direction that suits your strengths.
Whether you’re already based in Townsville or looking to make the region your home, we’d love to hear from you.
Our Culture, Our Difference
At Spiire, we believe our culture is our difference. As a successful and growing employee-owned business, we recognise and reward the contributions of our people and provide real opportunities and pathways for career progression.
Here’s a snapshot of what’s on offer:
 - 
 Structured training, knowledge-sharing forums and mentoring opportunities.
 - 
 Supportive leaders and clear pathways for career development.
 - 
 Collaboration with technical specialists across disciplines and offices.
 - 
 Health and wellbeing initiatives supporting physical, emotional, social and financial wellbeing.
 - 
 Extended leave benefits, including study leave and volunteer days.

 An inclusive, connected team culture with regular social and office events.
InSpiire to build something great
If this sounds like your next move, we’d love to hear from you.
For questions about the role or recruitment process, please contact Spiire.Careers@spiire.com.au.
Apply now or discover more about us at www.spiire.com.au.
Spiire is committed to creating a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace where everyone can thrive. candidates.content_text:
Build infrastructure that keeps Queensland moving!
Are you a civil engineer ready to apply your technical knowledge to meaningful transport projects? Join Transport and Main Roads and help plan, deliver and manage roads, bridges and other infrastructure that support safe and reliable travel across Central Queensland.
About the role
As a Civil Engineer, you will work with experienced engineering and project professionals across the full project lifecycle. You will contribute to transport planning, project development, design, delivery, maintenance and asset management activities, while building your capability under the guidance of senior engineering staff.
Central Queensland Region manages transport infrastructure across more than 600,000 square kilometres, including over 9,000 kilometres of state-controlled roads and 1,500 kilometres of the National Land Transport Network. With offices in Rockhampton, Mackay, Emerald and Barcaldine, the region offers exposure to varied infrastructure, environments and engineering challenges.
In this role, you will:
* provide technical engineering advice and undertake assessments to support planning, design, delivery, maintenance and asset management
* manage projects or project components to achieve quality outcomes, value for money and sound engineering practice
* identify project risks, emerging issues and opportunities, and develop practical and cost-effective solutions
* support procurement activities and the administration of consultant and construction contracts
* coordinate budgets, forecasting, accruals, procurement and performance reporting
* contribute to the delivery of road, bridge, maintenance and asset improvement projects
* build effective relationships with internal and external stakeholders
* ensure work meets relevant governance, safety, risk management and departmental requirements.
What you will bring
You will use sound judgement, take responsibility for the quality of your work and collaborate effectively to achieve project outcomes. You will be comfortable applying civil engineering and project management principles across multiple infrastructure projects, while actively developing your professional knowledge and capability.
You must hold:
* a four-year Washington Accord accredited Bachelor of Engineering in Civil Engineering, or an equivalent qualification accepted by Engineers Australia
* a current Class C driver licence.
Why join TMR?
You will gain hands-on experience across diverse transport infrastructure projects while working alongside experienced professionals. TMR supports career development, an inclusive workplace and a healthy work-life balance.
This role provides an opportunity to strengthen your technical, project management, commercial and stakeholder engagement skills while contributing to infrastructure that makes a practical difference for Queensland communities.
If you are looking for varied civil engineering work, professional support and the opportunity to contribute across the full project lifecycle, we encourage you to apply.
Applications to remain current for 12 months.             
Job Ad Reference: QLD/707063/26
Closing Date: Wednesday, 25 November 2026

Civil Engineer, Water
At Aurecon, we are optimistic about the future. We are thinkers, solvers, and collaborators who work with our clients to deliver the infrastructure and assets that strengthen communities and create a sustainable future.
What you'll do
As a Civil Engineer, Water in our Transport, Water, Environment and Land team, based in Perth, you'll contribute to projects and programs that make a real difference and be part of a team that embraces challenges, welcomes diverse ideas, and engineer solutions with people and outcomes in mind. What you'll do:
- Planning, design and coordination of piping systems for water and wastewater, pump stations, water distribution networks and treatment plants. Ability to understand or provide input to the development of hydraulics and water balance to inform decisions.
- Civil design of infrastructure including earthworks, concrete structures, access roads, and drainage systems.
- Preparation of detailed drawings, models, and specifications using design tools such as Water Gems, Sewer GEMS, Civil 3D, 12D, Open Plant, AutoCAD, QGIS, Microstation.
- Collaboration with multidisciplinary teams (e.g. mechanical, process, electrical, structural) to ensure integrated and constructible designs.
- Technical input during planning and feasibility stages, including constructability reviews, material selection, and cost estimates.
- Support during tender and construction phase, including site inspections, responding to queries, and ensuring designs are implemented correctly.
- Work within study and project teams to meet scope requirements and ensure time and budget objectives are achieved.
- Engage and build positive relationships with existing and potential clients and stakeholders, support business development and tenders to win and deliver work for Aurecon,
- Produce input to written reports, documents and presentations to explain engineering ideas and concepts.
- Support during tender and construction phase, including site inspections, responding to queries, and ensuring designs are implemented correctly.
What you'll bring
- Bachelor's degree in Civil, Mechanical, or Environmental Engineering (or a related discipline)
- 5+ years industry experience.
- Experience working in a consultancy environment, with a strong understanding of project delivery, client interaction, and commercial awareness.
- Experience coordinating with services and utilities.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving, innovation, and continuous improvement in design practices.
- Familiarity with 3D model space design.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills to convey civil engineering outcomes with suitable language that can be understood by clients, stakeholders and other engineering disciplines.
- Solid time management and organisational skills.
- Ability to collaborate effectively within multidisciplinary teams and communicate clearly with clients and stakeholders and produce quality reports.
- Desire to contribute, grow and develop the capability and experience of the water team whilst progressing your own career development.
How we support your growth
We believe your career should be a rewarding adventure. You will tackle some of the world's most complex infrastructure challenges, in an environment that supports your ambitions, where we hold ourselves, and each other, to the highest standards. Recognised by the AFR as a Best Place to Work in 2026, we embrace diverse perspectives, giving you the opportunity to make a real impact.
Who we are 
We are an engineering consultancy with more than 6,000 people across Australia, New Zealand and Asia. We believe the world needs people who can engineer possibilities; people who can create infrastructure that makes life better for people and the planet. That is why we are here - to bring ideas to life, the Aurecon way.
Ready for your next adventure?
If this sounds like your next step, we'd love to hear from you. We value diverse experiences and welcome applications for part-time or flexible working arrangements. For recruitment adjustments, contact

candidates.content_text:

Representing an established multidisciplinary engineering consultancy, I am looking to introduce a Civil Engineer to a team with a strong presence across the consulting engineering and built environment sectors.
The business has built its reputation around technical capability, quality project delivery and strong working relationships. It is a practice where engineers are encouraged to contribute, take ownership of their work and collaborate directly with experienced colleagues rather than simply becoming another number in a large organisation.
The culture is down to earth, with a genuine emphasis on supporting the people around you, enjoying the work and creating an environment where good engineers can do their best work.
The Opportunity:
An opportunity is available for a Civil Engineer with a background in land development to join the Sydney team.
The preference is for a Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) who is comfortable taking technical ownership of civil design and contributing to the delivery of development projects across NSW.
You will work across the civil engineering design process, with exposure to stormwater management, drainage, earthworks and associated infrastructure. The role offers the opportunity to contribute technically, work alongside experienced engineers and have a genuine influence on project outcomes.
While CPEng accreditation is strongly preferred, the business is also open to considering experienced intermediate engineers with relevant land development experience who are progressing towards chartership and greater technical responsibility.
Experience with TUFLOW modelling would be particularly advantageous.

- Undertaking civil engineering design across a range of land development projects.
- Developing civil design solutions for stormwater drainage, earthworks, roads and associated infrastructure.
- Undertaking hydraulic and hydrological modelling, including stormwater management and flood assessments.
- Preparing engineering calculations, technical reports, design documentation and supporting approval submissions.
- Coordinating with internal engineering disciplines, external consultants, clients and relevant authorities.
- Applying relevant Australian Standards, council requirements and engineering guidelines throughout the design process.
- Contributing to design reviews, technical discussions and the overall delivery of projects.
What We Are Looking For:
- A degree in Civil Engineering.
- CPEng accreditation strongly preferred, with consideration given to experienced engineers progressing towards chartership.
- A minimum of 5+ years’ experience within civil engineering consultancy, ideally with 3+ years in the land development sector.
- Sound understanding of civil design principles, stormwater management and drainage design.
- Experience using 12d and/or Civil 3D expected.
- Working knowledge of DRAINS and MUSIC is desirable.
- TUFLOW modelling experience would be highly regarded.
- The ability to work collaboratively, communicate technical information and take ownership of your work.
What's On Offer:
- $135,000 – $165,000 + Super, depending on experience and capability.
- The business offers a working environment with plenty to like:
- Flexible working: Hybrid arrangements and flexible start and finish times.
- A supportive team: Work alongside experienced engineers in an approachable, collaborative environment.
- A relaxed culture: A professional workplace without unnecessary corporate formalities.
- Team connection: Regular social activities and company events throughout the year.
- Professional development: Opportunities to broaden your technical experience and contribute to increasingly complex projects.
Importantly, flexibility is not just something written into a policy. The business is happy to have a genuine conversation about what works for you.

I'm David Hamilton, a Registered Architect who has transitioned into specialist recruitment across the architecture, engineering and construction industries.
Having worked within the built environment myself, I understand the technical nature of these roles and appreciate that choosing the right next move is about considerably more than a job title or salary.
My approach is straightforward. I take the time to understand both the opportunity and the individual, ensuring there is a genuine alignment between the two.

Click APPLY or send your CV in Word format to david@salexo.com.au.
For a confidential discussion, call me on (02) 9922 9622.

The role

You will be involved from tender through detailed design, construction and as constructed records, working closely with our process and design engineers so that every drawing set is accurate, coordinated and buildable. You will:

- Prepare tank, skid and fabrication drawings, along with valve, pump and instrument schedules.
- Prepare site layouts, pipeline and rising main alignments, long sections and services coordination drawings using Civil 3D.
- Draft P&IDs and process flow diagrams with our process engineers.
- Prepare electrical and control documentation, including single line diagrams, schematics, switchboard layouts and cable routes, under the direction of the Electrical and Automation Lead.
- Coordinate drawing inputs from suppliers, subcontractors and our civil and structural design partner.
- Prepare drawing sets for tenders, regulatory submissions, construction and as constructed records.
- Manage drawing registers and revision control, and help develop the CAD templates, blocks and standards for the business.

- Proficiency in AutoCAD, Civil 3D and Plant 3D is essential. Experience in Inventor or SolidWorks is an advantage.
- Construction experience is beneficial but not essential. It helps to understand how drawings turn into steel, pipe and concrete.

Operations Engineer 
Location: MidCoast NSW
Looking for more than just your next job?
 Join a team that's helping shape the future of the MidCoast while enjoying the perfect balance of meaningful work and an exceptional lifestyle on the Barrington Coast. Here, your contribution matters - to your community, your team, and your own future.
The Opportunity 
The MidCoast region is home to a diverse network of water, wastewater and recycled water treatment systems. This role provides an opportunity to apply your environmental and engineering expertise to the operational challenges that support these essential services.
As an Operations Engineer, you will work across the Water Management and Treatment department to identify environmental risks, strengthen compliance, support operational projects and improve the performance of Council's water and sewerage systems.
You will work closely with operational teams, contractors, regulators and internal stakeholders, providing practical technical advice and helping ensure Council's treatment systems meet legislative, environmental and community expectations. The role includes a combination of technical investigations, environmental assessments, contract management, data analysis, reporting and fieldwork across the MidCoast region.
In this role, you will:
- Provide environmental and operational engineering advice across Council's drinking water, wastewater and recycled water systems.
- Assess environmental risks associated with water and sewerage operations, including biosolids, liquid trade waste, odour, effluent discharge, sludge handling, chemical storage and erosion and sediment control.
- Prepare and coordinate environmental assessments for operational projects, including Reviews of Environmental Factors and Environmental Management Plans.
- Develop technical specifications, manage procurement processes and oversee service contracts relating to water and sewer operations.
- Analyse environmental monitoring and compliance data, identify trends and issues, and prepare reports with practical recommendations.
- Support the investigation and response to environmental incidents, including undertaking field inspections and out-of-hours sampling when required.
- Provide technical input into projects involving biosolids, liquid trade waste, water quality, wastewater and recycled water systems.
- Support operational teams with environmental compliance, site land management and the implementation of Council's drinking water quality management system.
- Work with regulators, contractors, consultants and internal stakeholders to resolve issues and achieve required environmental and operational outcomes.
- Represent Council's water and sewer services in sustainability initiatives, industry forums and benchmarking activities.
- Undertake fieldwork across the MidCoast region, including working at heights, near open water and across uneven or varied terrain.
- Contribute to the ongoing improvement of Council's water and sewerage operations, systems and processes.
What you'll bring
- A degree-level qualification in Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering or another relevant discipline.
- Experience working in environmental, water, wastewater, engineering, infrastructure or industrial operations.
- Experience preparing environmental assessments, technical reports, environmental management plans or similar documentation.
- Demonstrated experience in procurement, contract management and the development of technical specifications.
- The ability to analyse monitoring and compliance data, identify risks and trends, and develop practical recommendations.
- Knowledge of environmental legislation, regulatory requirements and compliance obligations relevant to water, wastewater or industrial operations.
- The ability to provide clear and practical technical advice to operational teams and other stakeholders.
- Demonstrated ability to build and maintain constructive relationships with colleagues, contractors, consultants, regulators and other stakeholders.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to prepare reports and communicate technical information clearly.
- The ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and contribute effectively as part of a team.
- A current Class C Driver Licence.
- A commitment to workplace safety, environmental sustainability, continuous improvement and high-quality service delivery.
What we offer?
We are committed to the growth of our employees and have a range of benefits available to support wellbeing and career development. Click here to find out more. 
Looking to relocate? From housing and transport to community connections and personalised support - discover a range of local services designed to make your move to the MidCoast region easier. Learn more here.
Salary: Commencing salary circa $89,400 - $107,200 p.a. plus superannuation. (dependent on skills and experience)
Civil Liability Allowance 3.5%
A vehicle arrangement will be made with the successful candidate for this role. Council will provide you with a leaseback vehicle for an annual fee calculated as 20% of the gross purchase price. This is a fully maintained vehicle for both business and full private use with no additional expenses in normal use.
Location: This position will be based at our Administration Centre in Yalawanyi Ganya at 2 Biripi Way, Taree. You may also be required to be based from other Council sites across the MidCoast Council region.
Tenure: Permanent, Full Time.
Closing date: Sunday, 29 November 2026 at 11:00 pm.
For questions relating to the position requirements please contact Tenille Lawrence-Haskew, Coordinator Water Quality and Process who is the hiring manager for this role. Tenille can be reached on 02 7955 7780 or at tenille.lawrence@midcoast.nsw.gov.au.
For enquiries regarding the application process contact Candice Plevey, Human Resources Business Partner who is the HR representative for this role. Candice can be reached on (02) 7955 7107 or at candice.plevey@midcoast.nsw.gov.au.
How to apply: 
- When responding to the questions below, please include detailed and relevant examples of your skills and experience. Using the STAR method can help you prepare clear and concise responses using real-life examples. For more information regarding the STAR method, please click on this link.
- Please avoid using AI to generate responses to answer the questions in your application.

- We will be in touch via email.
Our organisation
At MidCoast Council our people are our most important resource and we believe that we can only reach our full potential when you reach yours. This is the place for those who seek to play a role in the community and have an enthusiasm to learn and grow. Here you can make a real difference.
Our community is our customer and is at the centre of everything we do. We value, support and empower our people to deliver positive results for our community.
Right now, we are investing heavily in our organisation, and our people. Our Administration Centre is a state-of-the-art facility designed to inspire innovation, creativity and collaboration. The building has been named 'Yalawanyi Ganya' which means "sitting/meeting place" in the Gathang language of the indigenous people across the MidCoast Region.
About the MidCoast Region
From lakes and estuaries to white sandy beaches to world heritage mountain wilderness, the MidCoast region offers an attractive lifestyle for everyone. Our community is characterised by its welcoming attitude, growing economy and natural beauty. These are the pillars of the quality of life we value. 
Our commitment
At MidCoast Council we are committed to providing equal employment opportunities. Our aim is to provide all of our staff with an inclusive, safe and healthy working environment. We never discriminate on the basis of race, religion, national origin, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age or marital, veteran or disability status. If you have a disability and need to request any adjustments to assist with the application process, or to discuss workplace adjustments you may require, please contact the HR representative.
Council also recognises the skills and attributes of veterans and welcomes applications from ex-service personnel.

candidates.content_text:
The Organisation
The Australian Security Intelligence Organisation (ASIO) protects Australia and Australians from threats to their security. ASIO’s people are ordinary Australians but they do extraordinary things – they are our most important asset.
To be successful, we need talented people who are highly capable, dedicated, adaptable and resilient.
We seek to reflect the community we protect. ASIO is committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive environment, where all staff are valued and respected. We welcome applications from all eligible candidates, irrespective of gender, sexual orientation, ethnicity, religious affiliation, age or disability. We are culturally and linguistically diverse, language skills enhance our collective ability to protect Australia. Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples are encouraged to apply. We are secretive about what we do, not what we value.
At a time when Australia’s security environment is dynamic, diverse and degrading, our work is more important than ever. Join the mission and make a difference every day.
The opportunity
Are you seeking an exceptional career where you can contribute and make a difference to the security of Australia? ASIO’s Technologist Graduate Program is a dynamic and fast-paced 12-month program with intakes in early & mid-2028. The program will set you on a pathway for a career with purpose.
We are seeking university students who have completed their degree before the intake commences, or graduates from the past 3 years who are passionate about technology, continuous learning and working collaboratively to make a difference. On commencement as a technologist graduate, you will be assigned to one of the following streams:
- Science & Engineering
- Data & Analytics
- Information & Cyber Security
- Software Engineering & Development
- IT Platforms
During the 12-month program, you will complete 3 workplace rotations designed to showcase the breadth of work that ASIO undertakes. This work may include:
- Working with industry and domestic partners to investigate, implement and manage new capabilities, networks and technologies.
- Assist in data and AI lifecycle management from acquisition through to sharing and disposal, applying best practice AI and data‑governance frameworks.
- Collaborating with business users to develop high-quality, high-performance software solutions within an agile environment.
- Advancing unique solutions to exploit technically-collected data, including through the use of machine learning and neural networks.
- Reducing the attack surface and assure the ongoing security posture of IT infrastructure.
- Undertaking reverse engineering activities.
- Supporting cyber security investigations.
- Conducting forensic analysis of digital media.
- Providing technical collection capabilities, including telecommunications interceptions.
- Undertaking complex data analysis and innovative visualisation to aid investigations.
- Evaluating technical surveillance counter-measures.
- Engineering high-end mechanical and electrical solutions.
The program will equip you with the skills, experience and knowledge to undertake a wide range of technical roles and to establish a diverse and rewarding career at ASIO.
A merit pool may be created to fill future vacancies which have the same or similar requirements to this position. This merit pool will be valid for up to 18 months.
What you will bring
We are seeking candidates with the following attributes:
- Adaptability
- Curiosity
- Commitment to learning
- Honesty
- Integrity
- Problem solving
- Resilience
- Teamwork
We are seeking candidates with the following capabilities:    
- The ability to work collaboratively
- The capacity to think critically and laterally in solving problems
- The propensity to adapt to emerging issues, events and environments
- Personal qualities that exemplify ASIO’s values and expected behaviours.
Qualifications 
To apply for a graduate program in ASIO, you must have completed a relevant degree prior to program commencement, or no more than 3 years prior.
Candidates are required to have a degree which could include, but are not limited to:
- Cloud Computing
- Data Engineering, Data Science or Data Analytics
- Software or Computer Systems Engineering
- Cyber Security
- Network Engineering
- Computer Science
- Information Technology or Information Systems
- Digital Forensics
- Electrical/Electronic Engineering
- Mathematics or Statistics
- Telecommunications
- Data or AI Management
- Project Management or Business Analysis with an ICT focus.
What we offer you
ASIO provides a number of benefits to its staff including:
- A competitive salary, including a 7.5% allowance for maintaining a TOP SECRET-Privileged Access security clearance.
- Employer superannuation contributions of 15.4%.
- A variety of leave options in addition to the standard 4 weeks annual leave, including stand down between Christmas and New Year.
- Flexible working arrangements. Please note due to our unique working environment, work from home options are not available.
- Study assistance, including financial support and study leave for tertiary education.
- Access to 7 staff-led diversity and inclusion networks.
- Access to an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).
- Mentoring opportunities.
Eligibility 
To be eligible to work at ASIO, you must be:
- an Australian citizen
- have completed your degree before the program commences, or graduated in the past 3 years
- assessed as suitable to hold and maintain a TOP SECRET-Privileged Access (TS-PA) security clearance.
Location
Canberra, ACT.
We advertise positions nationally to reach the broadest audience. Please refer to the above location before applying.
Reasonable adjustments
Please let us know if you require any additional assistance or reasonable adjustments during any stage of the recruitment process in order to fully participate in the recruitment process or the workplace. This may include reasonable adjustments to assessment methodologies to enable full participation.
How to apply
ASIO officers’ identities are protected by law. Under section 92 of the ASIO Act, the only declared ASIO officers are the Director-General and Deputy Directors-General. Due to the need to protect our people’s identities, ASIO holds all employment applications in the strictest of confidence. It is essential that you do the same. Please do not discuss your application with others as doing so may adversely affect your potential employment.
Click on ‘Apply online’ to commence your application. Your application must be complete and include the following:
- Succinct responses to the questions below:- Tell us why you are interested in applying for the Technologist Graduate Program.
- Tell us about a technical ‘passion project’ you have been involved in. This can be a personal initiative, tertiary related or other. We want to understand what your technical interests are, what drives you and how you apply it. Feel free to be as technical as you like.
- In our workplace the rate of technical change means there is a premium on knowledge sharing. How important is learning and communicating to you?
- A current CV, no more than 2 pages in length, outlining your employment history, the dates and a brief description of your role, as well as any academic qualifications or relevant training you may have undertaken.
- A copy of your academic transcript. If you have not yet graduated, please provide your most up-to-date transcript. This can be an unofficial copy as long as it is issued by your tertiary provider.
- Details of 2 referees, which must include a current or previous supervisor. ASIO will not contact your referees without advising you prior to doing so.
Read the ASIO People Capability Framework and Core Capability Guide, available on ASIO’s website. Ensure your responses address the relevant capabilities and levels outlined in these frameworks.
Use of artificial intelligence in recruitment processes
ASIO does not use any form of artificial intelligence (AI) at any point in the recruitment process.
All applications are reviewed by a selection panel. We recognise some applicants may use AI technologies to draft applications or prepare for interviews. If you wish to use AI, we recommend doing this only for initial drafts and ensure that your application is personalised and accurately reflects your skills, experience and qualifications.
Additionally, be aware of the privacy policies of any AI tool you use. Be mindful of the information you are entering into AI tools (personal details, work history, etc) and how using it may link you to potential ASIO employment, noting that you are expected to be discrete and maintain confidentiality with your application.
If you are invited to attend interview, the use of AI tools and recording devices during interview is strictly prohibited. Should AI tools or recording services be detected, your application, and any future applications may be discontinued.
The recruitment selection process – timeframes
Our selection process is rigorous and extensive. All employment decisions and selection processes at ASIO are based on merit principles and candidates must be prepared to undergo various selection stages. The stages may include application assessment, eligibility checks, online testing, skills-based assessment and interview.
We ask all applicants for their patience throughout the process.
As we are recruiting for the early & mid-2028 Technologist Graduate Program intakes, candidates can expect the following timeframes for the recruitment selection process:
- - Program advertised October and closes Monday 30 November 
- Assessment centres will likely run in March 2027. 
Employment conditions
Employment is under the Australian Security Intelligence Organisation Act 1979. Conditions of service are similar to those applying in the Australian Public Service. We recognise entitlements accrued under the Public Service Act 1999 and provide for continuation of superannuation under the Commonwealth schemes. Salary packaging arrangements are also available.
Australian Workplace Equality Index
ASIO has achieved the Australian Workplace Equality Index (AWEI) Gold Standard in 2024, 2025 and 2026, recognising ASIO’s inclusion work and positive culture. ASIO was the first Australian intelligence agency to achieve this status.
For more information about ASIO, please visit: www.asio.gov.au.

candidates.content_text:
Graduate Hydraulics Engineer – Canberra
Start your engineering career with real projects, real responsibility and people who will back you to grow.
At Northrop, you’ll contribute to projects from the start, work alongside experienced engineers and be trusted with responsibility early in your career.
 - Work on real projects from the beginning
 - Learn directly from experienced engineers and owners of our business
 - Build your career with mentoring, development and exposure to diverse projects

 What we provide
 - A dedicated mentor and buddy, plus a strong graduate network
 - Monthly career conversations and structured professional development
 - Internal and external training, with financial support towards Chartership
 - Exposure to different projects, sectors and disciplines
 - Industry-benchmarked salary with annual reviews
 - Genuine flexibility, including hybrid working, flexible hours and alternative public holidays
 - Paid parental leave and wellbeing support
 - A supportive culture with regular social activities and company events
 There isn’t one Northrop career path. We’ll give you the experience, support and opportunities to build one that works for you.
What you’ll own
As a Graduate Hydraulic and Fire Engineer at Northrop, you will:
 - Design of Fire and Hydraulics services as part of a broader team within the Built Environment: Hospitals, Education Facilities, Sporting Facilities, Commercial Mixed Use Developments.
 - Exposure to design of wet fire systems, hot and cold water supply, drainage, wastewater and sewer systems within a building.

 - Assist in preparation of design documentation of hydraulic services.
 - Work on multi-disciplinary design projects liaising with Civil, Sustainability and Building Services teams.
 - Collaborate with external stakeholders including architects, developers, commercial builders and local/state government bodies
 You won’t just observe - you’ll contribute!
At Northrop, you’re not just another graduate - you’re our future.
Why Northrop
We’re employee owned, which means our people have a genuine stake in the business they’re building. Our leaders are accessible, decisions are made by people who understand the work and good ideas can come from anywhere.
For more than 50 years, we’ve worked across a diverse range of projects and sectors, with multidisciplinary teams across NSW, ACT, Queensland and Victoria.
We’ve also been recognised by Prosple as one of Australia’s Top 100 Graduate Employers, with graduate workplace awards across overall satisfaction, employee engagement, training, green initiatives and social responsibility.
What you bring
We’re looking for graduates who are curious, motivated and ready to learn. You’ll enjoy solving problems, collaborating with others and bringing new ideas to the table.
You don’t need to have your career mapped out. We’ll help you build the experience and confidence to discover where your strengths and interests can take you.
Who can apply?
You must be in your final year of study or have completed your university degree within the past year.
Next steps
We’d love to hear from you. Please submit:
 - Your CV
 - Your most recent academic transcript
 - A cover letter answering: - o Why would you like to start your career with Northrop?
 - o What strengths would you bring to your graduate role?
 - o What would you most like to learn or develop in the first few years of your career?
 To find out more about working at Northrop, visit our Careers page. (northrop.com.au/careers)
If this role isn’t quite right for you, you can also register your interest in future opportunities with Northrop via our EOI form.  
https://v2.forms.jobadder.com/f/WzDLJEnGePglWrqXoxNZ7A32Y
Northrop is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people of all genders, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, and people from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds. If you need adjustments to participate in our recruitment process, let us know and we’ll work with you.

candidates.content_text:
We’re on the lookout for experienced Site Engineers and Project Engineers to join our growing team and play an integral role delivering some of Queensland’s largest residential development projects across the beautiful Sunshine Coast.
 With multiple opportunities available, this is an exciting chance to join Shadforth, a leading Queensland civil contractor, and work on projects that are shaping communities and providing thousands of new residential lots across the region.
About you
 You’ll have a strong understanding of civil construction and subdivision works, excellent communication skills and a proactive approach to delivering quality outcomes.
 We’re looking for Site and Project Engineers with experience across civil construction, particularly those who have worked on residential subdivisions or major earthworks and infrastructure projects.
Key responsibilities will be:
 - Assist with the planning, programming and delivery of civil construction and subdivision projects.
 - Coordinate site activities to ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently and to agreed timeframes.
 - Monitor project quality, compliance and environmental requirements.
 - Assist with project cost management, forecasting and reporting.
 - Coordinate subcontractors, suppliers, procurement and site resources.
 - Work closely with Project Managers, Supervisors and site teams to achieve project outcomes.
 - Maintain strong relationships with clients, consultants and subcontractors.
 - Prepare and maintain project documentation, records and reports.
 - Identify and resolve project issues proactively.
 - Support the development and mentoring of junior team members.
 About you
 - Bachelor of Engineering (Civil) 
 - Minimum 2 years’ experience in civil construction for Project Engineer opportunities; relevant experience will be considered for Site Engineer positions.
 - Previous experience delivering residential subdivision projects will be highly regarded.
 - Strong understanding of civil construction methodologies, quality and safety requirements.
 - Excellent communication and organisational skills.
 - Ability to build positive relationships with clients, subcontractors and internal teams.
 - Strong problem-solving skills and a proactive approach.
 - Ability to work effectively as part of a high-performing project team.
 What's in it for you?
 - Company supplied vehicle + Fuel Card
 - Local Work | Enjoy the benefit of returning home each night, giving you more quality time with your family.
 - Job Stability | Leading civil contractor with ongoing pipeline of works  that are shaping cities and communities
 - Career Progression | Access to people and leaders to support and guide you through your career 
 - Supportive Environment | Work with skilled Supervisors who appreciate and acknowledge your efforts.
 - Wellness Programs | Regular programs offering Wellness and Awareness initiatives co-designed amongst the Shadforth Teams
 - Diversity & Inclusion | committed to fostering an inclusive and diverse workplace
 About Us
 Shadforth are one of Queensland’s largest family-owned civil construction companies originating on the Sunshine Coast over 60 years ago. We have a strong presence across Queensland and Northern New South Wales where we have developed an outstanding reputation working across many sectors including residential and commercial subdivisions and major civil infrastructure, including roads and bridges.
 To Apply
 Click 'apply now' to submit an up-to-date copy of your resume and a covering letter highlighting your experience or reach out to your recruitment team at 07 5458 3342 for a confidential conversation.
 Checkout our website for other career opportunities - www.shadcivil.com.au
